answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not yet on either one, but you are close. Next week stays easy at about 21 miles, with two short sets of strides to wake up your leg speed.

Feeling ready is a good sign. But legs often feel fine before the muscle damage from a marathon has fully healed, and that usually takes three to four weeks. Jumping from 12 to 40 miles in one week is the kind of spike that leads to injury.

If the Thanksgiving 10K is on, here is roughly how the next few weeks would go:

| Week | Miles | Speed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 26 – Nov 1 | about 21 | strides only |
| Nov 2 – 8 | 26 to 28 | one short session |
| Nov 9 – 15 | 30 to 32 | one session at 10K effort |
| Nov 16 – 22 | 30 to 34 | one sharper session |
| Race week | lighter | a short reminder at race pace |

You don't need 40 miles for a 10K that's four weeks away. With your marathon base, 30 to 34 miles and one good session a week is plenty.

Tell me three things: is the 10K definitely on, what is the date, and do you want to race it hard? Also tell me what you want after that, for example a spring marathon, so I can plan the winter.

new.analysis:
## Last week
You ran the plan exactly as written: four rest days, then easy runs of 3, 4 and 5 miles with no pain. Each run was a bit quicker at a slightly higher heart rate, and that's what recovery looks like.

| Run | Pace | Avg HR | How hard it felt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wed Oct 21, 3 mi | 10:49/mi | 128 | 4/10 |
| Fri Oct 23, 4 mi | 10:16/mi | 133 | 3/10 |
| Sun Oct 25, 5 mi | 9:51/mi | 139 | 3/10 |
| Tue Oct 13, 5 mi (before the race) | 9:52/mi | 139 | 3/10 |

By Sunday your easy pace and heart rate matched your runs from before the race. That tells me your heart and lungs have bounced back, so next week can go back to your usual five days.

## Why it stays easy
Your heart and lungs recover faster than your muscles and tendons. Two weeks ago stairs were hard, and that damage keeps healing for a while after the soreness goes. One more easy week costs you no fitness and makes it safer to start speedwork the week after.

Going from 12 to about 21 miles is still a real step up, so keep every run under 142 heart rate. That keeps you in zone 2, where your easy runs stayed all through the build.

## What the race taught us
Your 3:50 was 12 minutes faster than your first marathon, and you ran 8:30s through mile 20, slightly faster than 3:45 pace. Then your quads gave out and the last 10K slowed to about 9:30/mi. When the race moved two weeks earlier, you lost training time and only got one 20-miler in.

That points to two things for your next marathon: long runs that build more staying power, and steady strength work for the quads. Friday's strength session starts that habit now, while the running is light.
